lines: Daniel Mahncke and Shawn O'Malley explain why they doubled down on Mercado Libre: its tightly integrated e-commerce, logistics, payments and credit form a self-reinforcing moat that rivals like Shopee and Amazon struggle to replicate in Latin America.

Fintech (Mercado Pago and Mercado Credito) now makes up 43% of revenue and is growing faster than commerce; the hosts argue proprietary data such as merchants' sales history and shipping reliability lets it underwrite loans at lower risk than traditional banks.

They attribute the drop in operating margin from about 12% to 7% to upfront credit-loss provisioning and investment in logistics and free shipping, not to price wars or falling take rates, since expected losses on a fast-growing card book are booked before interest income arrives.
With Latin American e-commerce penetration at only 14-15%, they see room for several profitable players, noting both Mercado Libre and Shopee are taking share from weakening legacy incumbents.
The hosts also view the model as resilient to the region's political and economic swings, because it has turned weak local infrastructure into a competitive advantage.
